fixtures.justification: The twin cells synthtwin's generation method requires for the fourteen cases docs/spec/generation-method-v1.md section G14.3 adds beside its first nine, computed from that specification alone. This count read 'six' while the file held seven, and is corrected here with the eighth: the seventh is the month-span case of plan P4-D4.3, reaching the second resolution that names a span rather than an instant, and the eighth is long_tail_levels (residual R-P4-17), the first frozen case to reach any of the four roles Phase 4 added. It pins admission of a folded count above the categorical ceiling and the stand-in walk of G8.3, and it does not pin a generator branch belonging to the role, which is stated at that width in G14.3 rather than left to be discovered. The ninth is clock_ladder (residual R-P4-17), the first frozen case for time_of_day and the first for any role whose method section did not exist until it was written on 2026-08-27. Its ends are eleven seconds apart and eleven of its cells parsed, so the all-different repair of method G7A.4 has no slack and every interior rank must land on the one ordinal left for it; its mutant withdraws the step-up and the same column then writes two times twice. The tenth is affixed_brackets (residual R-P4-17), the first frozen case for affixed_number: it pins that the role's universal class counts answer for the CELLS while its quantitative block answers for the CORES, and that only the second set reaches the numeric rules. Its mutant hands over the cell counts and the oracle stops at the word budget, which G4.3 also reads over the cores. Every other case carrying n_distinct_values publishes the figure its own twin reaches, so none of them can exercise that miss. The eleventh is joined_readings (residual R-P4-17, which it closes), the first frozen case for joined_numbers and the one that pins method G6B.4's pairing walk, the only search in the method. Its column publishes a rank agreement of 0.4323, holds the earlier position above the later in only seven of twelve rows and repeats values in both positions, so the walk has real work: with its step 5 withdrawn, six of the twelve cells move, which is the registered mutant. Withdrawing each of the walk's other rules in turn moves its cells for six of the rules method G6B.4 states; five it does not reach are named in that section rather than left implied, and the rank origin is named as byte-invariant in either convention so no case can pin it. The walk does not converge here: it stops at its try ceiling at 0.2226 against the 0.4323 published, which the case records. All four roles Phase 4 added now have a frozen case. The twelfth is unrepresentable_exponent (residuals R-P4-48 and R-P4-68, which it closes with the landing that wrote method G10.5 revision 5): six cells of whole numbers too large for binary64 to hold, published at five and six characters wide -- widths no digit string can be written at, because a whole numeral needs 310 figures to be certain of leaving the format's range. It reaches the EXPONENT spelling family revision 5 adds, which unrepresentable_joint beside it cannot: every cell that case freezes is a four-hundred-character digit string or the fixed contradictory construction, so the family could have been withdrawn whole with both committed files byte-identical. Its mutant puts the too-large shape's floor back to the digit string's own 310 characters and the recount then reads min_length as 310 against a published 5. It is also the first case in either file carrying a positive and a negative group of one shape, which is what made the section state whether the spelling walk counts per shape or per shape and sign: two conforming programs could differ on that and agree on every byte committed before it. Four exist because review item P2-C3-F3 found that the nine reached no unrepresentable column, no joint class-and-alphabet packing of free text, no fold collision that a case change cannot build, and no cell carrying the literal decimal, leading-zero or leading-plus style; the fifth exists because review item P2-C4-C3 found that none of them carried a seconds field of 60, the one published end the ordinal space cannot hold. A defect or a withdrawn rule on any of those branches left every committed byte unchanged. This file is written by the same oracle as tests/reference/generation-reference-vectors.json, through the second entry point beside it, and shares that oracle's transform and its proof layer; it is a second FILE only because a committed fixture must stay under the 100000-byte cap and the nine cases already spend 88207 of it. Everything the first entry says of itself holds here: the vectors are a pure function of the uint64 words the file carries as inputs, the recorded seed is accepted and ignored, every binary64 published is proved correctly rounded or proved exact by integer comparison against the midpoints to its neighbours, and the run refuses a full-generator mutant before it writes a byte. The registered generator here is the second ENTRY POINT rather than the oracle itself, and its imports are stated literally (review item P2-C4-C4): it imports os, runpy and sys, and nothing else; it holds no transform and no proof layer of its own; and it executes the oracle beside it by one fixed sibling path, which is the file that imports only argparse, datetime, fractions, json, math, struct and sys. Neither file imports synthtwin, numpy or pandas. No value in this file comes from any real or synthetic table. schema_note: Fixture allowlist for the synthtwin data-provenance guard (plan D13). Each entry in 'fixtures' binds one committed data fixture to its origin and must contain exactly these keys: 'path' (repository-relative POSIX path of the committed fixture file), 'generator' (repository-relative path of the seeded script that rebuilds the fixture; invoked as: python <generator> --seed <seed> --out <output-path>), 'seed' (integer seed; the same seed must always produce the same bytes on every platform), 'sha256' (64-character lowercase hex digest of the committed fixture bytes), and 'justification' (a written sentence explaining why this fixture must be committed instead of being built at test time). The checker tools/provenance/check_provenance.py re-runs every generator and byte-compares its output to the committed file; any difference fails. Both 'path' and 'generator' must be repository-relative (no absolute paths, no '..' components), must stay inside the repository, and must be tracked by git once the repository has commits. Generators are executed through tools/provenance/guard_runner.py, which installs a Python audit hook before the generator code runs; the hook refuses imports of network, process, and native-capability modules and blocks the known socket, process-creation, and native-call audit events. That runner is a best-effort in-process guard, not a sandbox or a confinement mechanism: repository source review of every generator script and the CI checks are the operative controls (CI is the authoritative automated verification; from Phase 3's visibility flip the branch ruleset makes it a mechanically enforced merge requirement - see SECURITY.md's activation record). JSON is treated as a data format: a tracked .json file is allowed only if it is one of the checker's known configuration files (KNOWN_CONFIG_JSON in the checker) or listed here. Committed fixtures must be tiny; the cap is the checker's own MAX_FIXTURE_BYTES, which carries the record of what it was raised from and why. THIS SENTENCE HAS GONE STALE TWICE and is written as a growth list rather than a number so the next entry has an obvious place to be recorded: it named a cap of 100000 after the checker's had been raised, and it said THREE were committed while four stood in this file. Five are committed today: the numeric reference vectors of Phase 1, and the four files of the generation reference vectors, which are ONE oracle in four files because each must stay under the cap - the fourth added by landing 2b.17 for the transforms that produce a whole document rather than one column's cells. All five are mathematics rather than data - they contain no value taken from any table, and each generator imports none of the code the vectors check.
